entries.reason: Carl-approved (2026-09-15): inserts one new dd_unicorn_roles catalogue row (System Account) and reassigns unicorn_role/is_system_account for exactly 3 named accounts (admin@vivacity.com.au, angela+invitetest@vivacity.com.au, bulk-generate-automation@vivacity.com.au) already confirmed non-human/test/automation identities. bulk-generate-automation's real production capability is carried by a separate, untouched supplemental role -- this migration only reclassifies its primary role label. Carl-approved RBAC v6 capability scoping (2026-09-15): inserts one new permission_features row and 7 role_permissions rows for the new email_templates.manage key, modeled directly on the existing public.email_templates RLS boundary (Super Admin full, other internal Vivacity roles limited/view-only). The ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is a safe upsert guard, not a destructive operation on existing data -- these are brand-new rows for a brand-new feature key.

Verified zero effect on Vivacity's own tenant (6372), which has zero rows in this table already.

False positive: the flagged INSERT/UPDATE statements are inside CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bodies for get_user_notification_prefs/update_user_notification_prefs (only executed later, per-caller, when those RPCs run) - the migration itself performs no direct data mutation, only ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, and two function redefinitions. Carl explicitly authorized proceeding with the not-null fix after reviewing the tenant-assignment question separately (L10 #18, parked to docs/kb/reference/tenant-operating-model-data-architecture-plan-2026-09-02.md §18 item 14).

Carl explicitly authorized this scoped self-swap-guard hotfix (L10 #31) for review via the standard allowlist path after the scanner flagged the pre-existing function body as new text.

False positive, same shape as l10-31-swap-tenant-user-to-contact-self-guard and p4d-18-allow-tenant-less-notification-prefs above: the flagged 'UPDATE unicorn1.users' statement is inside the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION body for the new mark_unicorn1_user_mapped(bigint, uuid) RPC - it is not executed at migration-apply time, only later, per-caller, when the mark-unicorn1-user-mapped Edge Function invokes the RPC (gated on FeatureKeys.adminUnicorn1 via requireCaller, same as the existing search_unicorn1_users read-side function this mirrors). False positive, same shape as p4d-18/l10-31/l10-33 above: all flagged INSERT/UPDATE statements are inside the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bodies for start_client_package and transition_membership_state (package_instances/stage_instances/staff_task_instances/client_task_instances/email_instances/document_instances/client_audit_log inserts, package_instance_state_log insert, package_instances/tenants updates) - unchanged from each function's existing production behavior, only executed later, per-caller, when a SuperAdmin/staff user actually calls the RPC. The migration itself performs no direct data mutation; it only adds an app.user_can_access_tenant() authorization check ahead of each existing, unmodified body, revokes SELECT on two views, creates one new read-only SECURITY DEFINER RPC (get_package_burndown), and drops/recreates get_tenant_user_capacity without its spoofable p_caller_id parameter. Carl explicitly authorized all four fixes ("proceed on all four") after independent live re-verification of each finding by both Claude and Codex, then explicitly authorized the merge. See docs/audit-log/entries/2026-09-11-tenant-package-security-fixes.md.

Applied to production and QA with no pilot account or invite data seeded; the migration is covered by the Academy Solo audit entry.

Approved Academy Solo controlled-pilot provisioning: the SECURITY DEFINER RPC creates an isolated Academy tenant and writes the required audit event only when an authorized staff member starts the pilot flow. Applied to production and QA, verified with zero Academy Solo accounts or demo invites created during migration rollout.

Approved Academy Solo access boundary and lifecycle controls: update the tenant marker during explicit provisioning, write audit events for staff lifecycle actions, and revoke access for the single-seat Academy learner on lifecycle completion. Applied to production and QA; anon EXECUTE was explicitly revoked in the follow-up corrective migration and all pilot counts remain zero.
